subject: Undeclared allergen (gluten) in falafel mixture from Turkey, via the Netherlands
hazards_observed: The product was found to contain >640 mg/kg gluten. In addition, common wheat/spelt-specific DNA sequences were detected. According to Annex II of Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 (LMIV), ingredients and processing aids made from cereals containing gluten are to be classified in the category ‘Substances or products that cause allergies or intolerances’ under point 1 ‘Cereals containing gluten and products made from them’ and thus highlighted in the list of ingredients. The list of ingredients does not contain gluten. products causing allergies or intolerances’ under point 1 “Cereals containing gluten and products thereof” and must therefore be emphasised in the list of ingredients. No ingredients containing gluten are listed. The label also includes the notice “gluten free”. According to Regulation (EU) No 828/2014, the term ‘gluten-free’ may only be used if the gluten content is no more than 20 mg/kg. In addition, the ingredient sesame must be emphasised in the labelling.

Chronic iodine deficiency may result in the formation of nodules in the thyroid gland, particularly in older people. If these nodules are suddenly activated by an excess supply of iodine, as may occur in the case of seaweed products with an extremely high iodine content, the result may be an overactive thyroid (iodine-induced hyperthyroidism) with life-threatening effects on the metabolism.

subject: Chocolate-coated biscuit rolls with milk cream filling, with questionable veterinary control when imported from the Syrian Arab Republic
product: Chocolate-coated biscuit rolls with milk cream filling
hazards_observed: /// According to the list of ingredients, the product contains whole milk and components thereof and has been produced in Syria. Syria is not listed in Annex -I of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2021/405 and therefore does not have an approved control plan for residue monitoring of processed products of animal origin contained in composite products. Consequently, under Implementing Regulations (EU) 2021/405 and 2021/404, Syria is not a listed country for export to the EU of composite products containing milk. The rules for entry into the EU of composite products are set out in Articles 20-22 of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/2292. The biscuits are therefore not marketable in the EU. They most likely do not meet the import requirements of 2017/625.
